FR-001.title: The project object available to generated scripts MUST expose a read-only parser area alongside its existing areas, offering a plain parse, a structured parse, a trace, a reload and a currency read

FR-002.title: The parser area MUST NOT expose any way to record, file or otherwise write parse results, and the absence MUST be stated where a future contributor will read it

FR-003.title: Loading the parser component MUST be triggered by use, never by import, so a renamed or relocated installation degrades to parser unavailable instead of breaking import

FR-004.title: Before use the system MUST verify the parser component comes from the same installation directory as the data model in use, and MUST refuse otherwise; the check is directory equality only

FR-005.title: Before use the system MUST verify by inspection that every operation it intends to call exists, and MUST bind those operations positionally rather than by parameter name

FR-006.title: The detected parser version MUST be reported and MUST NOT be compared against any minimum; a standing test MUST guard this in each repository that probes

FR-007.title: Scripts MUST be able to read all genres assigned to a text, not only the first

FR-008.title: Scripts MUST be able to get the entry that owns an allomorph; the data model exposes the relationship, the script library never wrapped it

FR-009.title: Scripts MUST be able to read morpho-syntactic analyses without dropping to raw data-model access

FR-010.title: Parser results crossing into script-visible form MUST preserve the identity of the underlying lexical objects, not only their text

FR-011.title: The new surface MUST be released as a versioned package before the assistant-side work is tested against it; the declared minimum and bundled index must agree

FR-012.title: The assistant MUST offer a tool that parses one word and MUST expose all three levels of answer: restricted-to-a-hypothesis, plain yes/no, and full explanation. Each MUST reach the

FR-013.title: The plain yes/no level MUST NOT present itself as explaining a failure, and MUST point the caller at an explaining level instead.

FR-014.title: Guidance MUST steer callers to the restricted level when they have a hypothesis and to the full explanation only when they do not, since the full explanation is the expensive one a

FR-015.title: Every handler that reaches the parser MUST check the project's configured parser engine as its first action, before any parser is constructed, and MUST refuse a project configured

FR-016.title: A missing recording agent MUST NOT mark reading unavailable, since reading neither records nor needs one.

FR-017.title: The new tools MUST be annotated read-only-safe, and that annotation MUST be backed by a standing test asserting that a real parse loads no user-interface framework code into the pr

FR-018.title: The restricted trace MUST accept a decomposition expressed in terms a caller can actually write -- entry headwords, headword plus sense, or internal identifiers -- and resolve it t

FR-019.title: If any piece of a decomposition resolves to no usable analysis, the request MUST be refused, naming the piece, its position and its candidates, and no parse MUST be run.

FR-020.title: Lookup structures used for resolution MUST be built once per run and reused across words.

FR-021.title: Where every piece has exactly one unambiguous candidate, the system MAY offer a proposed decomposition; when it does, it MUST label it proposed and unverified.

FR-022.title: Guidance offered when a decomposition is missing MUST name only actions the caller can actually perform with the tools that exist.

FR-023.title: A caller's proposed decomposition MUST always be traced exactly as given. The system MUST NOT substitute a different restriction, widen it to an unrestricted search, reorder, score

FR-024.title: Where the system has something to say about a proposal, it MUST be limited to an adjacent candidate or a conflict with recorded analyses, MUST be worded as an observation rather th

FR-025.title: Agreement between a proposal and recorded analyses MUST produce no commentary.

FR-026.title: All parser execution MUST go through one run mechanism. There MUST NOT be a separate synchronous path.

FR-027.title: A run MUST report a distinct stage for starting, loading the grammar, parsing, filing (defined but unreachable in this checkpoint), completed, failed and cancelled.

FR-028.title: A run reaching a terminal stage inside a configurable grace window (default 5 seconds) MUST return its results inline; otherwise it MUST return a handle. The window governs reporti

FR-029.title: Results MUST be written to the run's record as they are produced, so a run that dies or is cancelled leaves everything completed so far readable.

FR-030.title: Runs MUST be ordered by the same priority levels and ordering the host application uses, lowest value first, first-in-first-out within a level, enqueued per word.

FR-031.title: A higher-priority single word MUST interleave at the running batch's next word boundary. The batch MUST NOT restart or lose position, the grammar MUST NOT be reloaded, and the batc

FR-032.title: Cancellation MUST be cooperative, stopping at the next word boundary and leaving a cancelled terminal stage over the partial results.

FR-033.title: The assistant MUST offer a read-only status tool taking a run handle and reporting stage, progress, and -- on a terminal stage -- the result summary or the failure with its guidanc

FR-034.title: A failed run MUST carry guidance pointing at the diagnostic instruments, since memory exhaustion is the case where a diagnosis beats a retry.

FR-035.title: A status request for an unknown handle MUST be refused naming the handle and the handles that do exist.

FR-036.title: A cancelled run MUST be reportable with the count of words completed and the stage it was in when cancelled. Reporting a cancelled run's status is not itself a refusal; the cancell

FR-037.title: Three refusal codes MUST be added additively to the existing tool response contract -- unresolvable morph, unknown run, and cancelled run -- with the documented count raised from 2

FR-038.title: Every piece of guidance shipped in CP1 that had to point at nothing because this tool did not exist MUST be revisited and pointed at it.

FR-039.title: Test groups deferred by CP1 MUST be brought into scope: the no-user-interface-code guarantee, the no-oracle case, the conditional-proposal case, and the script-library facade group

FR-040.title: Whether the three grammar lints deferred at CP1 are folded in here MUST be decided and, if deferred again, recorded as such. *(Decision D5.)*

FR-041.title: This checkpoint MUST NOT modify the capability check already shipped in this repository; the script library MUST probe the read operations its own surface binds

FR-042.title: At most one loaded grammar MUST be held at a time, for the project in use, and it MUST be released when another project's grammar is needed

FR-043.title: A held grammar MUST have its currency confirmed before reuse and MUST be reloaded when stale; a parse MUST NOT be served from a grammar whose currency was not confirmed

approach: CP2a adds a read-only parser area (project.Parser) to the flexicon package plus three read gaps (text genres, allomorph owning entry, MSA reads), then cuts a 4.9.0 release. The work is mostly pattern replication against settled flexicon idioms; the two genuinely new pieces are a capability probe that degrades with a reason (no template exists in the package) and a reload bound as reset-then-update rather than a bare update. It ends with a written A1-A3 evidence artifact, which is CP2b's entry gate -- not a passing test count.

decisions.decision: Re-tier evidence gate A1: run it with FieldWorks present and simulate parser-component absence, instead of the briefed no-FieldWorks/CI framing
decisions.why: import flexicon itself requires FieldWorks -- __init__.py:76 pulls in FLExInit, whose module scope calls InitialiseFWGlobals() and raises when the registry key is absent. The briefed A1 could not execute its first check. It was doubly wrong: no CI workflow runs pytest on a hosted runner, and the self-hosted windows+fieldworks pool has zero registered runners. SC-001 is unaffected -- it speaks about the parser component being absent, not FieldWorks.
decisions.rejected: Refactoring the package import chain so import flexicon works without FieldWorks -- a package-wide change entirely outside US1

decisions.decision: FR-009 wires the existing MorphosyntaxAnalysis wrapper and MSACollection rather than designing a new MSA read surface
decisions.why: Both classes are already complete in the package (morphosyntax_analysis.py:74, msa_collection.py:76) with full is_*/as_*/pos_* families, and are instantiated by no code path at all. The cycle-1 brief called MSA reads the nontrivial gap; that is right about the shape and wrong about the cost. Wiring template is AllomorphOperations.GetAll:104, the same two-subtype case already shipped end to end.
decisions.rejected: Designing a fresh flat MSA reader -- duplicates a tested surface and is wrong for a hierarchy whose subtypes expose different property sets

decisions.decision: Reload binds as reset-then-update (two steps); the parser CAPABILITIES token lands last, after tiers A1-A3 pass
decisions.why: HCParser.Update() is guarded by a conditional that short-circuits on an unchanged model, so a bare update would ship a discard guarantee that is fiction -- the exact shape of the RollbackToMark incident Constitution Principle I cites. Separately, test_capabilities.py:12-16 states a token added without a landed capability behind it is a Principle V violation, and the token is read across the repo boundary by FlexToolsMCP.
decisions.rejected: Binding Reload to Update and documenting the conditionality -- documenting that a required guarantee does not hold is a Principle V violation dressed as candour

decisions.decision: Allomorph owning-entry copies LexSenseOperations.GetOwningEntry (OwnerOfClass + null guard), not the three one-hop .Owner siblings
decisions.why: Three of the four existing GetOwningEntry siblings (Etymology, Pronunciation, Variant) take a single .Owner hop and are unguarded, so a null owner throws inside the cast. An IMoForm can sit under an affix-form chain where one hop lands on the wrong object. Constitution Principle I cites copying a working pattern without re-checking it on the target type as the documented root cause of issues #36, #39 and #40.
decisions.rejected: Copying the nearest sibling by file proximity -- AllomorphOperations sits in Lexicon/ beside the Variant and Pronunciation ones, which is exactly how the wrong template gets chosen

decisions.decision: E-B RESOLVED by the user at plan review: flextools_parse_status ALWAYS returns a success envelope on terminal stages, carrying state cancelled|failed. parse_job_cancelled fires only from calls that ACT ON a dead run; parse_run_not_found is the only error the status tool emits.
decisions.why: Asking about a dead run is a successful query, not a failed request. An error envelope carries no result payload by convention, which would make SC-008 partial-result readability unreportable through the very tool FR-033 provides for it. Confirms the spec as already written (D-04, amendment E8) -- no spec change required.
decisions.rejected: An error envelope for terminal runs, which costs SC-008 readability; and a split (success for cancelled, error for failed), which gives CP2b callers a two-branch rule to remember while SC-008 applies equally to both

decisions.decision: Exclude SIL.FieldWorks.WordWorks.Parser from the LCM contract scan (tests/contract/extract_lcm_contract.py NON_CONTRACT_PREFIXES) rather than adding HCParser to the contract baseline
decisions.why: The LCM contract asserts that every type flexicon imports resolves out of a REQUIRED library; TestLiveContractVerification reflects each one. ParserCore is deliberately OPTIONAL -- FR-003 makes its import function-local so import flexicon survives a missing component. Letting HCParser into the contract inverted that: the snapshot generator does not load ParserCore.dll so the type read as missing, and loading it would make a contract test require the very component the package promises to work without. Fixes three real failures (test_no_new_type_dependencies, test_all_types_found, test_compatibility_score). Parser surface existence is verified where it belongs -- tier A2 against the real installed component, and GetAvailability at runtime.
decisions.rejected: Adding HCParser to the contract baseline (test_all_types_found would still fail, it is checked against the liblcm snapshot); and teaching the snapshot generator to load ParserCore.dll (makes an optional component mandatory for the contract suite, contradicting FR-003)

decisions.decision: TraceWordXml binds analyses=None to NULL (not an empty array), refuses an empty sequence with FP_ParameterError, and clears a non-empty restriction before the next plain parse
decisions.why: Live tier A3 caught a silent wrong-answer defect. ParserCore ParseToXml branches on selectTraceMorphs != null: null REOPENS the morpher LexEntrySelector/RuleSelector, an EMPTY array installs a filter admitting nothing, and the selectors OUTLIVE the call while plain ParseWord never touches them. The facade was converting None into an empty array, so every unrestricted trace silently restricted the parser to nothing and left it that way -- a word parsing with 1 analysis returned 0 thereafter, with no exception. Read out of HCParser.cs, then reproduced and pinned live on IndonesianHC-Complete.
decisions.rejected: Reading an empty sequence as no-restriction (silently widens a restriction the caller asked for, answering a different question); and documenting the leak as a caller responsibility (ships a wrong-answer trap)
